title: Announcements are not scoped by event or audience at read time and lack pagination

original_titles.title: Announcements not scoped by event or audience

problem: GET /announcements selects audience but does not filter by the caller’s event/team/role or by the audience value. It returns up to a limit without cursor semantics. A participant may receive notices intended for another event/audience.
impact: Cross-event disclosure, accidental release of organizer-only notices, and incomplete history after the hard limit.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Define announcement audience semantics (all, participants, team, staff, organizer/admin) and make it a closed enum in the request model.
Resolve the caller’s event/team from principal membership; include event_id predicate and audience authorization predicate in the SELECT.
For team-scoped notices, join a matching team membership. For staff-only notices, check the role server-side.
Add cursor pagination and stable ordering, and include the visible audience/event metadata in the response.
Test cross-event, wrong-team, participant-vs-staff and pagination cases.

acceptance_criteria: No user receives an announcement outside their event/team/role audience.
History is paginated and never silently truncated.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
